clue.text: The part of the breadwinner?

parts.note: the role of a person who keeps a household going financially, read as an actor's part

explanation.surface: A question about what role the family earner plays.
explanation.walkthrough: A secondary part in a play or film is a supporting role; the breadwinner literally supports the family, so the whole clue reads both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor acting part beside the lead is so called, and the earner of a family plays the one that keeps everyone fed.

clue.text: Maybe it's through the hot water being switched on

parts.note: per means through or by way of, as in 'per post'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: switched means turned round, so the word for water is read backwards

parts.note: a spa is a place of mineral water

explanation.surface: Something about the boiler possibly heating once the hot water is turned on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being switched on' looks like plumbing, but it turns SPA backwards to APS, which follows PER and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are words of possibility, synonyms for 'possibly'.

clue.text: As soon as one lass had skipped class in it

indicators.note: it refers back to the word one, which takes the leftover letter inside it

parts.note: taken as the word itself

indicators.note: skipped means left out, so the letters of lass are dropped from the word class

explanation.surface: A girl skips school at the first opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing LASS from CLASS leaves C, which goes inside ONE, 'it' standing for that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a conjunction, the word means at the moment that, just like 'as soon as'.

clue.text: He keeps mum in order!

parts.note: a monk who keeps silent and belongs to a religious order, not a man disciplining his mother

explanation.surface: A man keeps his mother well behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' means silence and 'order' a monastic order: Trappist monks are known for their vow of silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this Cistercian monastic order are noted for observing silence.

clue.text: Count for the anaesthetist

definitions.meaning: to count is to total up a figure
read as one who numbs, a doctor deadening feeling

explanation.definitionFit: A figure is what one counts with, and someone who numbs a patient could jokingly be called by the same spelling.

clue.text: Rehearse the bit where you kill with the sword?

definitions.meaning: to practise a performance from start to finish

definitions.text: the bit where you kill with the sword?
definitions.meaning: to pierce someone completely with a blade

explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal from start to finish shares its name with stabbing someone right through with a blade.

clue.text: They submit to being put in a box

definitions.text: They submit to being put in a box

parts.words: They submit to being put in a box
parts.note: items of post that are dropped through a slot into a postbox, not people meekly accepting confinement

explanation.surface: People who meekly accept being shut up in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submit' suggests yielding; the things really go into a letterbox or postbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Items of correspondence are posted through a box's slot.

clue.text: When the shouting has to stop

definitions.text: When the shouting has to stop

parts.words: When the shouting has to stop
parts.note: in a British pub, 'shouting' is buying a round of drinks, which must end when the bar shuts

explanation.surface: The moment when the noise must end.
explanation.walkthrough: In British and Australian slang to 'shout' is to buy a round; a pub stops serving at a set hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The hour a British pub stops serving drinks bears this name.

clue.text: Declare yourself to be supportive of the demand

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a claim is a demand for something as due

explanation.surface: Announce that you back the demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to announce publicly.

clue.text: Crooked Italian I lost twice in South Africa

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
the letter I is to be taken twice

parts.note: taken as the letter itself

explanation.surface: A dishonest Italian lost twice while in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' rearranges ITALIAN once two I's are 'lost', leaving TALAN shuffled to NATAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a province of South Africa, now part of KwaZulu-Natal.

clue.text: Me, as often as not!

parts.note: the two letters given form one part of a two-part word for a duration, so they are a fraction of it

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they are themselves only some of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is the second half of TIME, and 'as often as not' is the plain meaning of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on about every other occasion means doing it as often as not.

clue.text: A means of getting off

parts.note: a way is a means or method

explanation.surface: Somebody looking for a method of escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of departure: gone off is gone elsewhere.

clue.text: Amazed at getting only a walk-on role?

definitions.meaning: so astonished as to be lost for words
a non-speaking part has no lines

explanation.definitionFit: Being dumbstruck and having no lines in a play are both lacking spoken words.

clue.text: Fightingto get a booking

explanation.definitionFit: A battle with the enemy and a performer's booked appointment share the word.

clue.text: A speed that's a defence against the enemy

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rapidity and a fortified stronghold.

clue.text: Is worn, as it happens

definitions.meaning: a garment that is put on the body

explanation.definitionFit: A hat is put on the head, and events take place, both covered by the phrasal verb.

clue.text: To her, appear to be hiding one object of value

indicators.note: hiding means concealing within, so the pair of words takes the letter for one inside

parts.note: taken as the word itself
I is the Roman numeral for one
to loom is to appear, especially menacingly

explanation.surface: Somebody seems to her to be concealing a valuable item.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes inside HER, giving HEIR, before LOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A family treasure passed down the generations is a prized possession.

clue.text: Soldier in a terrible rush because retreating

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
terrible signals that the letters of rush are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word for because is read in reverse

parts.note: as means because

explanation.surface: A soldier in a dreadful hurry as he falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SA (AS read backwards, from 'retreating') inside HUSR, an anagram of RUSH signalled by 'terrible'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalryman of a light horse regiment is a kind of soldier.

clue.text: New places-one in particular

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: New locations, one of them in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean distinct or individual, synonyms.

clue.text: A cat taken aback after the large ice plant

indicators.note: after places these pieces following the ice

parts.note: a berg is a large mass of floating ice

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word for cat is reversed

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A cat is startled by a large piece of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise but reverses TOM to MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus tree and an aromatic herb of the mint family both bear the name.

clue.text: From Dresden nemesis unfortunately comes

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Retribution comes from Dresden.
explanation.walkthrough: Meissen is a German town near Dresden famous for porcelain, often called Dresden china.
explanation.definitionFit: The porcelain made near Dresden is widely known as Dresden china, so things from there carry this name.

clue.text: Shocked and given a rude awakening

explanation.definitionFit: Being badly upset and being jolted awake are both a jolting, literal or emotional.

clue.text: "Don't worry," the soldier repeated

indicators.note: repeated means the pair of pieces appears twice

parts.note: taken as the word itself
RE is the Royal Engineers, a soldier in crosswords

explanation.surface: A soldier says 'Don't worry' over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing phrase of comfort used to reassure someone upset.

clue.text: Taking a strong line in business

explanation.definitionFit: The word means resolute and also a company.

clue.text: Abraham Lincoln, to start with, was murdered

parts.note: Abe is the short form of Abraham

indicators.note: to start with means take only the opening letter of Lincoln

explanation.surface: Abraham Lincoln was assassinated, a fact of American history.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names what happened to the biblical figure: the brother killed by Cain, and Lincoln was also murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam's son was slain by his brother Cain, the first killing.

clue.text: I am going through the additional material

indicators.note: going through means passing inside, so the letter I sits within the word for additional

parts.note: more means additional or extra

explanation.surface: Someone is going through the extra fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A watered silk fabric is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Mothers will be more familiar with than others

definitions.text: Mothers will be more familiar with than others

parts.words: Mothers will be more familiar with than others
parts.note: echoes the saying that mums are wiser than anyone else

explanation.surface: Mothers know things better than other people.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'Mother knows best' supplies the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wiser than anyone else is to be the one who is most informed.

clue.text: The fairest of the fair?

parts.note: the fair sex is women, and the fairest hair is a very pale silvery shade

explanation.surface: A question about who is the most beautiful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' means both blonde-haired and beautiful; a platinum blonde has the palest hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with silvery-white hair has the lightest hair of all.
